_meta.note: Facts taken from official docs via page-to-markdown summarisation; 'not documented' = not found on the pages fetched. Inferences are labelled INFERENCE.

Q1.answer: Two forms. A full-page database is a standalone page in the sidebar; an inline database is a block embedded in another page (it also appears as a subpage in the sidebar). A database is made of one or more 'data sources' (a set of pages); a database must have at least one data source.

Q2.answer: Yes. Use the /database slash command (or choose Table on a new page) to create an inline database among text blocks. A full-page database can be turned into inline by dragging it into another page, then block handle -> 'Turn into inline'; the reverse is dragging the inline block into the sidebar.

Q3.answer: Owned: 'Every item you enter into your database is a Notion page'; pages created in the database make up its data source. Membership is not a query over all pages. Rows can also be linked into other databases only via relation properties (see Q4).

Q4.answer: Not documented as a first-class feature: pages say a page belongs to its database; docs do not say a page can be a row in two data sources. The documented way to surface one page in another database is a Relation property (two-way relation syncs both sides without duplication). INFERENCE: one owning database + relations/linked views, no multi-ownership.

Q5.answer: Yes. 'Linked database' (/linked, 'Linked view of database') shows the same data source in other pages. Filters, sorts and groups set on a linked instance 'only apply to the linked instance' and do not affect the original; edits to rows made in a linked view change the original data. Each view has its own settings, not applied to other views. Linked sources inherit the access level of the original database.

Q6.answer: Data sources can be moved; moving a data source to another database adds it as that database's data source, moving it to a non-database page creates a database there. Inline database block can be moved/duplicated/copied-link via the block handle. Behaviour of rows when the containing page is moved: not explicitly documented on pages fetched (INFERENCE: sub-content moves with the page). Only users with edit access can move data sources.

Q7.answer: Deleted pages go to Trash and stay 30 days before permanent deletion (then a further 30 days retained but inaccessible to users). Archiving a parent page archives all child pages. When restoring a page that holds an inline database, the user can choose whether to restore the database's pages and properties. Behaviour of rows when a standalone database is deleted: not explicitly documented on pages fetched (INFERENCE: rows are its child pages and go to Trash with it). Behaviour of linked views when the source is deleted: not documented.

Q8.answer: Properties are defined per database (per data source), shown as columns on each page-row. A relation property links two databases; no global property registry is documented. Items can only belong to one data source so the two-collections-different-properties conflict is not documented.

Q9.answer: Not documented in detail. Help docs only say that on mobile you can toggle between a database page's views; which layouts are supported and how inline tables render on phones is not documented on the pages fetched.

Q10.answer: Offline mode: pages marked available offline are dynamically migrated to a CRDT data model for conflict resolution (official engineering blog). Specifics for database rows/properties (e.g. last-writer-wins) not documented.

Q11.answer: Table, board, timeline, calendar, list, gallery, chart (help article lists 7 layouts; chart = bar/line/donut). Each view has its own filters, sorts, grouping, visible properties.

Q12.answer: Create one Tasks database and one Projects database, link them with a Relation property, then on each project page add a linked (filtered) view of Tasks filtered to that project, so only relevant tasks show. Notion's own guide describes this pattern; the exact 'relation contains This page' filter UI is not detailed on the help pages fetched (community/template practice; the API doc for relation filters is at developers.notion.com).

Q1.answer: A base is a view over notes. It lives either as its own .base file or as a 'base' code block (YAML) inside a Markdown note. Data is not stored in the base: it stays in the local Markdown files and their properties (YAML frontmatter). Only formulas are defined in the .base file.

Q2.answer: Yes. Embed a base file with ![[File.base]] (specific view: ![[File.base#View]]), or write a ```base code block with YAML filters/views directly in the note. Command palette 'Bases: Insert new base' also exists.

Q3.answer: Pure query over all files: global and per-view filters (concatenated with AND) such as file.hasTag("x"), file.folder, property values, file.hasLink(this.file) (replicates backlinks). No owned children. 'Adding a note from a base with pre-populated properties' not documented on pages fetched.

Q4.answer: Yes by construction: a note is a file; any number of bases can match it via their filters; no duplication.

Q5.answer: A .base file can be embedded in many notes (![[File.base]]); a base holds one or more views each with its own filter (per-view filters AND global filters), sort, group. Edits to note properties from any view change the underlying note, so they show in all bases. Embedding a single view: ![[File.base#View]].

Q6.answer: Not documented on pages fetched. INFERENCE: a .base file is an ordinary file, so moving it moves only the definition; rows (notes) are unaffected because membership is by query. A base code block moves with its note text.

Q7.answer: Not documented on pages fetched. INFERENCE: deleting a .base or the note holding a code block deletes only the query; notes are untouched (handled by the vault's file trash settings).

Q8.answer: Note properties are stored in each note's YAML frontmatter (per note, vault-wide property names); formula properties are defined in the .base file. No per-database schema; a note keeps all its properties regardless of how many bases show it.

Q9.answer: Not documented on the Bases pages fetched.

Q10.answer: Not documented for Bases (plain files; conflict behaviour depends on the sync method used, e.g. Obsidian Sync - not covered here).

Q11.answer: Table, list, cards, kanban, map (map needs the Maps plugin); more layouts via community plugins. Grouping by a single property is supported; multiple sorts supported.

Q12.answer: Embed a base in the project note and filter with this: when a base is embedded, 'this' points to the properties of the embedding file, so a filter like file.hasLink(this.file) or a property link to this.file lists the notes (tasks) that link to / reference the project. Same base file can be embedded in every project note.

Q1.answer: Three constructs. Type = blueprint and built-in query of all objects of that type. Query (Set) = saved rule-based view over objects. Collection = container of hand-picked objects ('closest thing to a folder'). Queries and collections appear as objects in the space and can also be embedded inline.

Q2.answer: Yes: 'Inline Query' and 'Inline Collection' blocks embed them in pages; view edits in the block are local to that block.

Q3.answer: Query/Set: rule-based over Types (one or several) or Property-based sources (e.g. all objects with a tag); auto-updating. Collection: manual membership. Types: automatic by object type.

Q4.answer: Yes. 'The same Object can live in multiple Collections at once'; removal from a collection does not delete the object. Objects also appear in any number of queries/types views. No duplication.

Q5.answer: Yes. Queries/collections can be embedded in several pages. Each view carries its own filters, sorts and layout; changes to an inline block's view affect only that block; edits to the underlying objects reflect system-wide.

Q7.answer: Deleting a Query or Collection does not affect the underlying objects. Deleted objects go to the Bin indefinitely (no auto purge); restoring keeps previous links, types, properties and templates. Behaviour of a page containing an inline query/collection when deleted: not documented (INFERENCE: the block goes with the page, member objects unaffected). Deleting a Type with objects prompts to delete or keep the objects.

Q8.answer: Properties (relations) are independent entities in the space, reusable across Types (e.g. Genre on Books and Movies). A Type lists its properties; an Object may carry a property that is not part of its Type. Changing an object's Type retains its properties. Removing a property from a Type keeps values; moving it to Bin removes it from all types in the space. Types are per Channel(space).

Q9.answer: 'Not all views are available on mobile.' Which ones: not documented on pages fetched.

Q10.answer: Any-Sync is local-first and CRDT-based; objects can have multiple 'heads'; a new change references all heads, merging branches into one state; conflict resolution happens on-device; works offline.

Q11.answer: List, Grid, Calendar, Kanban, Gallery, Graph (views page); queries doc also lists Timeline. Filters (AND-joined) and multiple sorts per view.

Q12.answer: Make an Object-relation property (e.g. Project) on the Task type; on the project object embed an Inline Query over type Task with a filter on that relation. Docs describe the building blocks (inline query + per-view filter by property); a specific 'project shows its tasks' walkthrough was not found in the pages fetched. Alternatively an Inline Collection of hand-picked tasks.

Q1.answer: A query is a block: simple queries {{query ...}} (insert with /query) or advanced (datalog) queries written inside a block. No database object; data are pages/blocks with properties in Markdown/Org files.

Q2.answer: Yes: a query is itself a block placed among other blocks on any page (/query).

Q3.answer: Query over everything: filters include page, property, task, priority, page-property, page-tags, all-page-tags, between (journal dates), sort-by, with and/or/not. Page properties live in the first block of a page; block properties in any other block.

Q4.answer: Yes by construction: any block/page matching a query appears in each query result; no duplication.

Q5.answer: Query results are not a shared object: the same query text must be placed in each page (no named, shared view documented in the pages fetched). Each query block is independent. Edits to result blocks affect the source blocks (INFERENCE; not stated on the fetched page).

Q6.answer: Not documented on pages fetched. Properties docs do not cover moving pages.

Q7.answer: Not documented. INFERENCE: deleting a page with a query block deletes only the query text; results are other pages/blocks. Deleting a page deletes its .md file.

Q8.answer: No schema: properties are free key:: value text on a block/page, not declared per database; properties are case-insensitive, lowercase; alias and tags are built in. Values can be text, page links, tags.

Q9.answer: Not documented. The docs only note that full-text queries are 'only enabled on the desktop app at the moment'.

Q10.answer: Not documented on pages found (official Sync page returned 404 in the docs repo). Community sources only.

Q11.answer: Not documented on pages fetched for file-based Logseq (results render as list or table per query-table option - community knowledge, not verified).

Q12.answer: Put a query on the project page, e.g. a query on tasks that reference the page ([[Project]]) or with (property project [[Project]]) and (task TODO DOING). Operators and filters are documented; no specific 'project shows its tasks' recipe was found in official docs.

Q1.answer: Object type = category; opening a type shows all its objects in database format. A Collection is a manual group within one object type. A Query is a saved filtered view and is itself an object type (basic types include Page, Tag, Image, Weblink, Audio, PDF, Files, Tweet, AI Chat, Query, Table).

Q2.answer: Yes. Queries can be embedded in objects with /query or by linking an existing query and setting the view to Embed. Collections can also be embedded on pages.

Q3.answer: Type: every object belongs to exactly one type. Collection: manual and curated within one type. Query: automatic rule-based over object types, collections, tags/backlinks, search terms, properties, exclusions.

Q4.answer: Yes. An object can be in several collections ('multiple overlapping groups without duplicating content') and appear in any number of queries. It has exactly one object type.

Q5.answer: Saved/named queries (Capacities Pro) can be reused, pinned to dashboards or embedded across multiple pages. Whether view edits are independent per embed: not documented on pages fetched. Edits to objects are edits to the objects themselves.

Q7.answer: Collection deletion: not documented. Deleting an object type: delete button in the type settings (effect on objects not described). Trash behaviour for objects: not in the glossary excerpt.

Q8.answer: Properties are defined per object type and apply uniformly to all objects of that type; not shared across types. Labels = type-specific; Tags = cross-type. Object-select properties link types, with optional two-way linking between custom types only. Conversion between types maps properties. Because an object has one type, the two-collections-different-properties case cannot arise (collections are within one type).

Q9.answer: Queries can be created and edited on phones/tablets; on narrow screens the editor fills the page, wider screens show editor beside results. Rendering of embedded results on phones: not documented beyond that.

Q10.answer: Offline-first. The docs page says a version conflict makes the user choose local or server version and the other is deleted (no automatic merge); the product's changelog later says changes now merge automatically across devices. The two statements conflict; treat current behaviour as automatic merge per release notes, details not documented.
Q10.source: https://docs.capacities.io/misc/offline-support ; https://capacities.io/help (search-result summary of release notes; not verified)

Q11.answer: Queries: results shown as Objects, Blocks, or Objects and blocks, sortable, groupable, limit; the docs fetched do not name layouts. Release notes mention Tables, Kanban view and card views. Calendar/timeline not documented on the pages fetched.

Q12.answer: Set the task's Context (object) property to the project. The project page then shows the task in its embedded Tasks tab via backlink query; filter the tab to Open. Alternatively embed a query with a variable filter 'This object' so it adapts to whichever object embeds it.
